question.problem: The eighth and ninth terms of an arithmetic sequence are $65$ and $73,$ respectively. Determine the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by  

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,
$$

so we need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

Since the terms ${a}_{8}=65$ and ${a}_{9}=73$ are consecutive, we can subtract them to find the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{9}-{a}_{8} \\  & =73-65 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use one of our known values, say, ${a}_{8}=65,$ to determine the first term of the sequence. Since ${a}_{8}$ is $7$ jumps after ${a}_{1},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{8} & ={a}_{1}+7d \\ 65 & ={a}_{1}+7\cdot 8 \\ 65 & ={a}_{1}+56 \\ 65-56 & ={a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =9+(n-1)\cdot 8 \\  & =9+8n-8 \\  & =8n+1\end{aligned}
$$
